result:
The review of w130 found one problem to fix now, so the result is `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` and the work-item goes to you. `work start` (r22) and setting an initiative to `done` on `work withdraw` and `work resolve` (r23) are in, and the five w130 scenarios pass when I run them. Nothing under `features/` changed, no test was removed or weakened, and the one setup-only test change the implementer reported holds.

**To fix now (Important): `work retry` never sets the initiative to `done`** (`scripts/workqueue.py:195-208`). A retry can put a work-item back to `green`, like this:
1. `work run` moves the work-item to `green` and commits.
2. The push fails, so it moves the work-item to `failed` "from whatever status it has" (`supervise_faults.py:78-85`).
3. `work retry` returns it to `green`.

If that was the initiative's last open work-item, the initiative stays `started` and nothing later marks it `done`. That goes against r23 and against your answer (reading B), which names retry as one of the commands that set `done`. The implementer's reason for leaving retry out ("cannot make the condition true") misses this path. The fix is to give retry the same check withdraw already has, with `initiative.md` in the same commit. I found this by reading the code. I didn't build a reproduction, because faking a failed push needs commands this review can't run.
